newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols creep up before Friday.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols creep up before Friday.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. interest rate futures firmed slightly ahead of two key economic reports Friday.
Volatility for June Treasury bond options has been trying to rebound since sinking to contract lows earlier this week, bond floor analysts said.

On Thursday, June edged up to 8.60 percent late in the session, from 8.54 percent at the previous settlement, despite more narrow-range trading in the underlying futures. May climbed to 8.00 percent from 7.92 percent.
Ten-year note volatility rose to 5.45 percent from 5.40 in June and to 4.94 percent from 4.83 in May.

Supporting vols is anticipation of Friday's producer price and retail sales data. A Reuters poll of economists pegged March PPI unchanged overall and up 0.1 percent excluding food and energy. March retail sales are forecast up 0.6 percent.
In bond options, a U.S. bank bought 2,000 May 106/107 put spreads at a premium of 20/64 and a brokerage firm paid 44 basis points for 500 June 106 puts.
The focus was also on puts in the Eurodollar options market, where a large buyer of short-dated mid-curve June 93.00 puts set the tone for the session, traders at the CME said.
June mid-curve volatility rose 0.6 point to 15.50 percent on the day, while September was unchanged at 15.50 percent. Mid-curve options expire in 1997 but are priced from 1998 futures.
Volatility for June quarterly options also increased, gaining 0.5 point to 7.50 percent.
Other months were unchanged, with September estimated at 10.20 percent, December at 11.80, March at 13.00, June 1998 at 14.10 and September 1998 at 15.20.
Eurodollar market participants also were seen buying June 94.00 puts against sales of June 92.75 puts, selling May 94.00 puts and selling December 93.50 puts.
